To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CD36 family proteins Cameo2 and Scavenger receptor class B15 (SRB15) are the first identified non-internalizing receptors for lipophorin-bound carotenoids and that Cameo2 exhibits specificity for lutein and astaxanthis and SRB15 exhibits specificity for β-carotene.
the Y, C, and F loci encode the proteins CBP, Cameo2, and SCRB15, respectively.

the silkworm cocoon-color mutant genes encode proteins involved in the carotenoid uptake pathway from the gut lumen into the silk gland and that Cameo2 can distinguish the chemical structure of carotenoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the carotenoid delivery system in the middle silk-gland epithelium of B. mori.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of tissue-specific carotenoid delivery in the silkworm, as well as with the elucidation and application of the molecular mechanisms for the production of natural pigments in the silk gland of the silkwworm.
the molecular genetic analysis of the silkworn carotenoid transport pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the silkworm cocoon color mutants provide an excellent model system for studying carotenoid metabolism and the transport of carotenoid molecules.
the Y, C, and F gene products function in concert to transport carotenoids from lipophorin to the middle silk glands, thereby controlling cocoon coloration.

the Y gene encodes a cytosolic carotenoid-binding transporter in the middle silk-gland epithelium, and the C and F genes function as non- internalizing lipophorins receptors in the middle-silk gland epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a tissue-specific transport system exists for the carotenoids in the silkworm, and that the CD36 family proteins Cameo2 and/or SCRB15 are involved in this system as the receptors of carotenoid-lipophorin complexes in the middle silk glands.

the silkworm has a tissue-specific carotenoid delivery system, in which Cameo2 and Scavenger receptor class B type 15 (SCARB15) are involved in the uptake of lutein from circulating lipophoron and β-carotenes from circulating lipophron and the gut lumen, respectively.

the carotenoid-binding proteins and CD36 family proteins are involved in the tissue-specific delivery of carotenoids to the middle silk glands, and that these two proteins are responsible for the formation of the yellow, orange, and red cocoon colors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carotenoid-binding proteins in Bombyx morilipophorin and the middle silk gland are responsible for the tissue-specific delivery of carotenoids.

the CD36 family proteins Cameo2 and Cameo1, which are expressed in the middle silk glands, are involved in the uptake of lipophorin-bound carotenoids, such as zeaxanthin, lutein, and astaxanthins, in the silkworm.
the carotenoid delivery system in insects is more complicated than previously thought, with tissue-specific transport systems being involved in the delivery of carotenoids to the middle silk glands.
